newsitem.title: INDIA: Five pro-government militants killed in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Five pro-government militants killed in Kashmir.

text.p: Separatist guerrillas shot dead five pro-government militants in India's troubled state of Jammu and Kashmir, police said on Friday.
They said the members of the Ikhwan-ul-Muslimoon group were killed on Thursday night in the town of Sumbal, 29 km (18 miles) northwest of the state's summer capital of Srinagar.
"All those killed were residents of the Nasabal area of Sumbal. Police are investigating the case," a police spokesman said in Srinagar.

The Sumbal area is a stronghold of the Ikhwan-ul-Muslimoon, a group of former separatist guerrillas now supporting India. More than a dozen militant groups are fighting New Delhi's rule in Jammu and Kashmir, the only Moslem majority state in mainly Hindu India.
At least three pro-India militia groups are helping Indian paramilitary troops combat the separatists in the state.
According to an official, 537 people were killed in 159 bomb explosions and other militant-related violence in Kashmir during the first three months of this year.
More than 20,000 people have been killed in seven years of separatist violence in the Himalayan region.
